source.title: PURE O-SEQUENCES: KNOWN RESULTS, APPLICATIONS AND OPEN PROBLEMS

accepted.question_text: Determine the largest integer t such that every pure O-sequence of type t is unimodal, without imposing any restriction on codimension or socle degree. In particular, the paper highlights the unresolved special case of proving that every type-2 pure O-sequence is unimodal in arbitrary codimension.

evidence.quote: What is the largest type t for which all pure O-sequences are unimodal (indepen- dently of the codimension or socle degree)? Even proving that t ≥ 2, i.e., that pure O-sequences of type 2 are unimodal in any codimension, would be very interesting.

accepted.question_text: For a fixed codimension r, determine the largest integer t such that every pure O-sequence of codimension r and type t is unimodal.

evidence.quote: For a fixed codimension r, what is the largest type t for which all pure O-sequences are unimodal?

accepted.question_text: For a fixed codimension r, determine the largest socle degree e such that every pure O-sequence of codimension r and socle degree e is unimodal.

evidence.quote: For a fixed codimension r, what is the largest socle degree e for which all pure O-sequences are unimodal?

accepted.question_text: Determine the smallest codimension r for which there exists a nonunimodal pure O-sequence of socle degree 4.

evidence.quote: What is the smallest codimension r for which there exists a nonunimodal pure O-sequence of socle degree 4?

accepted.question_text: For fixed socle degree e and large type t, determine the asymptotic behavior of the number #P(*, e, t) of pure O-sequences of socle degree e and type t, including its order of magnitude.

evidence.quote: Determine asymptotically the number #P(∗, e, t) of pure O-sequences of socle degree e and type t, for t large. What is the order of magnitude of #P(∗, e, t)?

accepted.question_text: Determine the smallest number n of variables for which there exists a nonunimodal pure f-vector, equivalently a nonunimodal f-vector of a pure simplicial complex. The paper notes this after recalling Stanley's original nonunimodal example and later bounds for special cases.

evidence.quote: What is the smallest number of variables n (i.e., the number of vertices of the complex) allowing the existence of a nonunimodal pure f-vector?

A. Tahat [76] has recently determined the sharp lower bound n = 328 for nonuni- modal Cohen-Macaulay f-vectors of socle degree 5 (the socle degree of Stanley’s original example), and has produced examples in larger socle degree with n as low as 39.

accepted.question_text: Decide whether every matroid f-vector is unimodal or even log-concave, and whether every matroid h-vector has the analogous property. The paper records that representable matroids were known to satisfy these properties, but leaves the general case open.

evidence.quote: Stanley’s Twenty-Fifth Problem for the year 2000 IMU Volume “Mathematics: frontiers and perspectives” [70] asks, among a few other things: are all matroid f-vectors unimodal, or even log-concave? What about matroid h-vectors?
as a consequence of their work, log-concavity (hence unimodality) is now known for all f-vectors (see Lenz [42], 2012) and h-vectors (Huh [36]) of representable matroids.

accepted.question_text: Is every pure O-sequence of type 2 unimodal in arbitrary codimension? More generally, for each fixed codimension, which socle types force unimodality of all pure O-sequences in that codimension?

evidence.quote: A natural question is whether all pure O-sequences of type 2 and arbitrary codimension are unimodal. Also, for any fixed codimension, it is an interesting problem to determine which types force unimodality.

accepted.question_text: Does the Interval Conjecture Property for pure O-sequences hold in important unresolved cases such as codimension three, and more broadly what is the exact scope of the Interval Property for pure O-sequences, pure f-vectors, and related classes of sequences?

evidence.quote: While the ICP remains open in most instances — e.g., in three variables —
As for pure f-vectors, the IP is still wide open, and little progress has been made so far.
In general, at this time it is still unclear what the exact scope of the Interval Property is, and if it can also be of use in other areas of combinatorial algebra or even enumerative combinatorics.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a Steiner quintuple system S(4, 5, 21)? Equivalently, is the sequence (1, 21, 210, 1330, 5985, 1197) a pure O-sequence?

evidence.quote: The smallest value of r for which the existence of S(4, 5, r) is currently open is 21. In other words, it is unknown whether (1, 21, 210, 1330, 5985, 1197) is a pure O-sequence.

accepted.question_text: Classify all finite projective planes, or at least determine all integers q that can occur as their orders. In particular, the paper highlights the unresolved existence of a projective plane of order q = 12, which is equivalent to the existence of a corresponding pure O-sequence.

evidence.quote: A major open problem in geometry asks for a classification of all finite projective planes, or even just of the possible values that q may assume.
The case q = 12 is still open.

accepted.question_text: Is every matroid h-vector a pure O-sequence? Equivalently, does Stanley's conjecture hold for all matroid complexes, beyond the low-dimensional cases proved in the paper and cited work?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.4. Any matroid h-vector is a pure O-sequence.
However, the conjecture remains open in general.

accepted.question_text: Extend the asymptotic enumeration result proved for socle degree 3 to higher socle degrees: for fixed e at least 4 and large type t, determine the asymptotic behavior of the number of pure O-sequences of socle degree e and type t.

evidence.quote: Nevertheless it would be very interesting to extend the above results to socle degree e ≥ 4.

trace.notes: Resolved zbMATH 6153310 to the matching arXiv PDF 1204.5247 and mapped the paper structure. The PDF contains a dedicated Section 5 titled 'Open problems' on pages 16-17, with additional explicit unresolved questions in Sections 2-4.
Collected explicit open questions from Section 2 on unimodality thresholds and the Interval Conjecture Property.
Collected open combinatorial questions from Section 3 on Steiner systems, finite projective planes, and matroid h-vectors.
Collected the asymptotic enumeration question from Section 4, including the explicit extension request for socle degree at least 4.
Extracted the seven numbered open problems listed in Section 5 and used them as the canonical forms for several deduplicated items.
Rewrote the numbered open problem on unimodality by type into a standalone form and inlined the special type-2 case emphasized by the authors.
Kept the earlier type-2 question separate because it is an explicit finer-grained subproblem stated independently in Section 2, not merely a duplicate of the broad threshold question.
Merged the closely related Interval Property questions into one canonical item covering pure O-sequences, pure f-vectors, and the paper's scope question.
Expanded the statement about S(4,5,21) to include the equivalent pure O-sequence formulation supplied by the paper.
Expanded the projective-plane question to include both the global classification problem and the singled-out unresolved case q = 12.
Used the paper's explicit conjecture statement as the canonical wording for the matroid h-vector problem.
Deduplicated broad open problems against earlier contextual mentions while preserving separate narrower subproblems when they added distinct mathematical content.
All accepted items are self-contained, use only source-supported claims, and include verbatim evidence with page numbers from the resolved PDF.
